requirement_ref.quote: Repeated failed attempts must not allow brute-forcing an account.

test_objective: Repeated wrong passwords stop the account being brute-forced.
preconditions: the account exists and has no prior failed attempts against it

test_data.name: throwaway_account
test_data.description: a registered account this test may render unusable

steps.actor_intent: arrive at the sign-in screen as an unauthenticated visitor
submit the wrong password repeatedly, up to the threshold agreed in Q-1
make one further attempt past the threshold

outcomes.statement: The further attempt is refused by the protection agreed in Q-1, and the user is told what happened.
Supplying the CORRECT password during the protection window still does not sign the user in.
outcomes.note: The outcome that decides whether the protection is real. A limiter that waves through a correct password protects nothing, and a test that never tries it would pass against exactly that bug.

not_verifiable_yet: Whether the limit is per-account or per-IP — distinguishing them needs a second source address the executor does not have.
Whether the protection expires correctly after the stated window — needs either a clock the test controls or a wait too long to sit in a smoke run.
